headline_answer: Allowed, one per 100 ft of lot width
unit: mooring device + 1 PWC lift; 6.5 ft max height
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale lets you put davits, hoists and boat lifts on a seawall or dock, but counts them: one mooring device for each 100 feet of lot width, plus one lift used only for a personal watercraft. The device itself is capped at 6.5 feet above lot grade with a one-square-foot cross section, and a raised boat's lowest point may sit no more than one foot above the seawall cap. A permit from Development Services comes first.
detail_rows: Allowed where :: Boat davits, hoists and similar mooring devices may be erected on a seawall or dock - ULDR Sec. 47-19.3(b). Mooring devices are defined to include boat davits, hoists and boat lifts - Sec. 47-19.3(a)(1) | How many :: One mooring device for the first 100 feet of lot width or portion of it, and one for each additional 100 feet. A second device on a lot wider than 100 but under 200 feet needs Site Plan Level II approval by the development review committee, which looks at neighbours' views and the device's height, width and length - Sec. 47-19.3(b)(1) | Jet ski lift :: In addition, one lift designed and used solely for a personal watercraft is allowed per development site - Sec. 47-19.3(b)(2) | Size and height :: The davit, hoist or other device may not exceed one square foot in cross section or 6.5 feet above lot grade - Sec. 47-19.3(b)(3) | Boat when raised :: The lowest appendage of the vessel may not be hoisted more than one foot above the seawall cap, or above average grade where there is no seawall - Sec. 47-19.3(b)(4) | Covers :: No boathouse, permanent covering or temporary covering for a boat is allowed within the zoning setback area, and none may be placed over a public waterway - Sec. 47-19.3(g) | Projection :: The code sets no separate reach for the lift itself; it goes on the seawall or dock, and docks and similar mooring structures may extend 25% of the waterway width or 25 feet, whichever is less, from the property line. Moored boats may extend up to 30% of the canal width - Sec. 47-19.3(c); Code Sec. 8-91(e) | Principal building first :: Davits, hoists and similar mooring structures may only be built on a lot that already has a principal building and abuts a waterway - Sec. 47-19.3(c) | Permit :: A permit from the Development Services Department is required before erecting boat davits, hoists or similar mooring structures; on navigable waters every regulating agency must also approve, and the applicant must own the waterfront land or have the owner's written consent - Code Sec. 8-91(b) | Guide pole :: Any part of a lift that can be submerged needs a vertical guide pole at least 1.5 inches in diameter, standing at least 6 feet above the water at all times, with a reflective finish - Code Sec. 8-91(d) | Melrose Park and Riverland Road :: In these annexed areas a boat lift may not exceed 15 feet in height, must stay 10 feet from side plot lines and may extend no more than 33% of the waterway or 25 feet; lifts more than 5 feet out need night reflectors - ULDR Sec. 47-39.A.1.b(11) | Broward County :: Boatlifts and davits are listed among the projects that qualify for a county general environmental resource license, which the code says is issued within ten days of a complete application - Broward County Code Sec. 27-336(a)(1)f. | State and federal :: Floating boat lifts and floating vessel platforms that meet s. 403.813(1)(s), F.S. (they float at all times, hold the vessel out of the water, and either sit inside a previously permitted slip or total no more than 500 sq ft - 200 sq ft in Outstanding Florida Waters - beside a qualifying dock or bulkhead) need no state permit; a local government may then ask only for a one-time registration unless the platform is attached to a bulkhead with no dock. Structures in navigable waters otherwise need Army Corps authorization unless exempt or under a general permit - 33 CFR 322.3(a).
source: City of Fort Lauderdale ULDR Sec. 47-19.3 and 47-39.A.1.b(11) (Supp. 58 Update 2) and Code of Ordinances Sec. 8-91 (Supp. 67 Update 2); Broward County Code Sec. 27-336 (Supp. 72); s. 403.813(1)(s), F.S. (2026); 33 CFR 322.3(a)
notes: Height of the lift is measured from lot grade, not the seawall.

headline_answer: Allowed; 7.5 ft side setback
unit: seaward side yard setback for davits
qualifier: Miami Beach has no stand-alone boat lift section; its code treats davits and hoists as marine structures. In single-family districts a davit or any marine structure must keep a 7.5-foot seaward side yard setback, and how far it may reach is set by the projection limits in the city's marine-structures chapter - 10% of the canal width, 15% (up to 40 feet) where the waterway is wider than 100 feet.
detail_rows: Allowed :: The city's definition of marine structure includes docks, seawalls, piles, davits, hoists and similar structures - Code Sec. 66-4 | Side setback :: Seaward side yard setbacks for boat slips, decks, wharves, dolphin poles, mooring piles, davits or structures of any kind may not be less than 7 feet 6 inches, for new and enlarged structures; no boat may be moored so that it projects into that setback, and no mooring is allowed along either side of the walkway from the seawall to a dock - Resiliency Code 7.2.2.3 (RS districts), item 12; 7.5.3.2 for other districts | Projection :: Structures of any kind may not extend more than 10% of the canal or waterway width from the seawall; where the waterway is wider than 100 feet, 15% up to 40 feet. Residential lots on Biscayne Bay or waterways over 1,000 feet wide may go to 125 feet with state and county approval. A moored boat may not project beyond these limits - Code Sec. 66-113(a) | Over 40 feet :: A marine structure or equipment, attached to a dock or not, that projects more than 40 feet or beyond Sec. 66-113 needs state and county review; next to the WD-1 or WD-2 district it also needs planning board conditional use approval - Resiliency Code 7.2.2.3 item 12; 7.2.21.5; Code Sec. 66-113(a) | County sets the reach :: The maximum projection of a marine structure is determined by the county environmental resources department - Resiliency Code 7.2.2.3 item 12 | Permit :: Permits come from the building department, the state internal improvement fund or any other agency with jurisdiction, and Army Corps approval where the structure abuts navigable streams - Code Sec. 66-113(b) | Not in the code :: No lift height, raised-boat height, canopy rule or per-lot count appears in the city code or Resiliency Code text reviewed | Miami-Dade County :: Any work in, on or over tidal waters needs a county permit from the Department (DERM). A single-family boat lift, davit or floating dock that protrudes no more than 25% of the waterway width may use the short-form application, as may installing a boat lift or davit on a dock, seawall or bulkhead - Miami-Dade Code Secs. 24-48(1)(d), 24-48.2(I)(A)(2), (8), (20). | State and federal :: Floating boat lifts and floating vessel platforms that meet s. 403.813(1)(s), F.S. Structures in navigable waters otherwise need Army Corps authorization unless exempt or under a general permit - 33 CFR 322.3(a).

headline_answer: Allowed except in the Inlet
qualifier: Boca Raton has its own boat lift section. A lift is allowed in any waterway except the Boca Raton Inlet, may reach 25% of the canal width or 20 feet - measured with the lift fully raised - whichever is less, and must sit at least 10 feet from the neighbour's property line. Past 20% of the canal width only wood pilings may be used, and every lift must be designed by a state-registered engineer.
detail_rows: Where allowed :: Any waterway other than the Inlet - Code Sec. 22-63 | Reach :: In the fully raised position, 25% of the canal or waterway width or 20 feet, whichever is less. Beyond 20% of the width only wood pilings may be used and no part of the lift may stick out past the face of the pilings nearest the canal centre - Sec. 22-63(1) | Exceptions to the reach rule :: It does not apply in the Hillsboro or C-15 canals, which follow South Florida Water Management District rules, or to a lift beside a finger pier or dolphin that goes no further out than that pier or dolphin - Sec. 22-63(1); Sec. 22-69 | Side setback :: At least 10 feet from the property line of the adjacent lot - Sec. 22-63(2) | Reflectors :: The outermost lift pilings need a reflective band about 6 inches wide, about 2 feet below the top - Sec. 22-63(3) | Prohibited :: Where the lift would create a navigation or safety hazard, or where the site abuts a marsh, swamp or mangrove area - Sec. 22-63(4) | Design :: Lifts must be designed by a state-registered professional engineer; plans must show the waterway section, soil type, piling length, embedment and load capacity, wood treatment and fastenings - Sec. 22-64 | Compared with docks :: A dock may project only 6 feet into a waterway under 100 feet wide, 8 feet if wider, so the lift limit is separate and larger - Sec. 22-58(1) | Not in the code :: No lift height, raised-boat height, canopy rule or per-lot number appears in Chapter 22 | State and federal :: Floating boat lifts and floating vessel platforms that meet s. 403.813(1)(s), F.S. (they float at all times, hold the vessel out of the water, and either sit inside a previously permitted slip or total no more than 500 sq ft - 200 sq ft in Outstanding Florida Waters - beside a qualifying dock or bulkhead) need no state permit; a local government may then ask only for a one-time registration unless the platform is attached to a bulkhead with no dock. Structures in navigable waters otherwise need Army Corps authorization unless exempt or under a general permit - 33 CFR 322.3(a).

headline_answer: Allowed; up to 28 ft out (raised)

qualifier: Pompano Beach treats davits, hoists, vessel lifts and jet ski platforms as mooring structures, which need both a City Engineer engineering permit and a building permit. On waterways wider than 50 feet a lift may reach 28 feet in the fully raised position; on narrower canals it may go out as far as the navigational channel. No roofs or covers of any kind are allowed over a waterway, and nothing may be built on top of the seawall cap.

Docks on North Lake and South Lake have their own 22-foot limit and permit route.

It treats boat davits as a structure that needs a building permit - the fee schedule prices docks and boat davits together - and docks, piers and wharves need Army Corps approval and a channel at least four feet deep at mean low water.

The jet ski lift is limited to 3,000 pounds and two mooring pilings, and a small boat may sit on it only if it has no rigid canopy above the gunwale. Covered boat lifts are not permitted at all, lifts in canals must run parallel to the bulkhead, and lifts must respect the district side setback.

headline_answer: Allowed; up to 3 per house
unit: 25 ft from bank; 75 ft channel kept
qualifier: Coral Gables permits davits, watercraft lifts and floating watercraft lifts as residential accessories after an administrative site plan approval and certified engineering drawings. A single-family home or duplex may have any combination of one set of davits, one lift and one floating lift - three in total, or four with a second set of davits on 200 feet or more of waterfront. Lifts may not reach more than 25 feet from the bank and must leave at least 75 feet of navigable waterway.

headline_answer: Allowed; lift and lift cover need a building permit
qualifier: Lantana requires a building permit before a boat lift or boat lift cover is built, put up or structurally altered. The application needs a scaled survey in duplicate showing the dock the lift attaches to, the size of the lift or cover and where it sits on the dock. Residential docks themselves are capped at 1,000 square feet, 25% of the water body and 100 feet, and must keep 25 feet from neighbouring property lines.

headline_answer: Allowed by type; pontoon lifts banned
qualifier: Key Colony Beach regulates each kind of lift. Davits need a concrete base 5 feet from the property line and an engineer's certificate, and over 5,500 pounds need city commission approval. Elevator lift forks may reach 12 feet into the canal, lift up to 31,000 pounds and never rise above the seawall cap. Other lifts, including cradle lifts, need commission approval, and hydro or pontoon lifts are prohibited.
